          Names written in one place, and Troubleshooting as plugins. Naming gains the {scope} token and a Server Policy (plugins) section for the names Plugin Studio flows build, and Classification › Name scope is the one place its value is written, per zone; spo-fortiweb 1.4.0 and the native New Server Policy wizard both take it from there. Network Segments carry one interface per network and segments or networks can be cloned. The six Troubleshooting pages are Plugin Studio apps under Plugins › Troubleshooting, Scout is a top-level sidebar entry above Wiki, and Sentinel's architecture page explains Scout and Path Diagnostics. Fixes from the nightly review, including pyasn1 0.6.5.

          Added

          • Sentinel's architecture now explains Scout and Path Diagnostics. Request: "Scout, which helps operations, and Path Diagnostics: in Sentinel I do not see how they work, their architecture or how they decide; this must be there." /sentinel/docs and the Settings › Sentinel › Architecture pane gain three cards:
          • 13: Sentinel, Path Diagnostics and Scout side by side, a flow diagram and their NAF blocks.
          • 14: Path Diagnostics' ladder, verdict rules, border verdicts, decision criteria and metrics context.
          • 15: Scout's live state (tools, default provider, external gate, round budget), what it decides, proposes and never does, its trail, tool catalog, log sources and source statuses. Everything comes from the enforcing code: scout_ladder, scout_config.criteria(), scout_metrics, advisor.tools_catalog(), and the new scout_sources.BUILTIN_SOURCES / SOURCE_STATUSES. search_logs asks the sources in that order. _src refuses a status the table does not explain. advisor.PROPOSAL_EFFECT and views.advisor.APPLY_GATE are now the one table _can_apply reads. The provider's base URL is not shown. The Open Scout and Open Path Diagnostics links follow those pages' own gates. Tests: tests/test_sentinel_ops_doc.py.
          • Naming: the publication scope {scope}, and one place for the names plugins build (FA-0011; request, translated: "I use spo-bv-host-port, spo-ext-host-port or spo-all-host-port depending on where it is published, and that comes from the rules of the 'New FortiWeb server policy (DDI + certificate)' plugin -- change the naming or do everything in plugins?"). Decided: Administrator › Naming defines the pattern, the flow decides the values. {scope} is a new site token (reserved, readable by a variable); an EMPTY scope takes one adjoining dash with it, so spo-{scope}-{host_u} with no scope is spo-shop_example_com and every pattern saved before renders exactly as it did. New FortiWeb section Server Policy (plugins) (server policy, virtual server, VIP, server pool) with the tokens a Plugin Studio render_names step passes ({extra}, {service}, {dns}, {spo} below the policy) besides the site tokens and the variables; its defaults (spo-{scope}-{extra}-{service}-{port}, vs-{spo}, vip-{spo}, pool-{spo}) give exactly the names spo-fortiweb 1.2.x gave. The page has a Scope picker next to the sample address and shows, under every pattern that uses {scope}, what it gives for none / bv / ext / all. The render_names step gets Name patterns from (patterns, as before, or naming) and Shipped patterns: with naming the four names come from Naming and the step's Patterns only add other objects (e.g. service); a Patterns row for one of the four that is not one of the app's shipped patterns and gives another name stops the step (move the pattern to Naming, delete the row) -- an install that customised its data store is never renamed in silence. A SATOM without this ignores both settings and uses the Patterns. Tests: tests/test_naming_scope.py.
          • Classification › Name scope: the ONE place the {scope} of a name is written (follow-up to FA-0011; request, translated: "it should be possible to write it somewhere, not depend on a plugin -- add a section in Classification; if it is on the scope is added, otherwise not; these things always have to be variables, never hard-coded"). New section on Administrator › Classification: a switch Add the scope to names, one value per zone of the zones catalog and one for More than one zone, with the Server Policy (plugins) name each gives for a sample site, rebuilt by the render_names step's own code while you type. A site published in one zone takes that zone's value, in more than one zone the "More than one zone" value; empty, or the switch off, no scope. Values follow the safe-name rule; a refused save writes nothing and hands your values back; a renamed zone keeps its value, a deleted one loses it. There is no built-in value anywhere: nothing saved = off. Migration nscope01 writes the values ONCE for an install that already runs spo-fortiweb, from its spo-fortiweb-rules store (the split rule's zone ext, more than one zone all, internal none -- the names 1.2.x gave), so no name changes; set bv on Internal on the page if that is your convention. The render_names step (naming mode) gets Publication zones and takes the scope from there; a scope in its values is ignored. The native New Server Policy wizard takes the scope of the zone of the appliance it builds on, so a {scope} in its patterns names the site as the plugin would. The Naming page's Scope picker offers the values saved here instead of a fixed bv / ext / all. spo-fortiweb 1.4.0 passes the zones of its FortiWeb rules and has no scope column any more (1.3.0's was never published). Tests: tests/test_name_scope.py, tests/test_naming_scope.py.

          Changed

          • Network Segments: one interface per network, and rows can be cloned (FA-0010; request: "the Networks column has a field for the interface, but there is still another Interface field in the next column — confusing; also make the lines clonable"). The segment-level Interface column is gone: every network line carries its own CIDR, gateway and interface. Nothing is migrated in place and nothing changes for a VIP: settings_store. normalize_networks (the one reader) gives a network stored without an interface the segment's stored interface, so the page shows it and the next save writes it into the network; the segment's scalar interface now mirrors its first network, like cidr/gateway (a segment with no network keeps its stored value). A stale cached page or a hand-built POST that still sends seg_interface[] fills the networks that name none, default port1 as before. New copy buttons clone a segment row (name + -copy) or a single network line; a new network starts on the interface of the one above it. The New Server Policy plan no longer prints the segment-level "on " next to the network list, which already names each network's interface. Tests: tests/test_segment_networks.py.
          • Troubleshooting is a Plugins submenu: its six pages are Plugin Studio apps (request: "every element in Troubleshooting as plugins, loaded, and also in the Builder ... they go in the Plugins menu"). Backend Reachability, Config Compare, HTTP Observatory, Path Diagnostics, Transaction Tracer and Diagnose Log Collection are six signed plugins (backend-reachability, config-compare, http-observatory, path-diagnostics, transaction-tracer, diagnose-log-collection, menu group Troubleshooting); imported and published they are Plugins › Troubleshooting, and the sidebar no longer draws the old Troubleshooting entries (partials/nav_troubleshooting.html removed). The pages keep answering by URL. Each app is ONE new SATOM step over the code its page runs (services/studio_troubleshoot.py: reach_check, config_compare, observatory_scan, path_walk, txn_trace, log_collect), so the verdicts, saved reports, audit line (via: plugin studio) and limits are the page's; each step asks the person who runs it for the page's permission and runs in the run's ADOM, and none is a write kind (the tracer never sends POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE in a rehearsal). The tracer's /run and the log collection's /collect now call one function each (views.txn_trace.trace, views.logs.start_collection) shared with the steps. New form-list source fortianalyzer (Path Diagnostics' analyzer). Tests: tests/test_studio_troubleshoot.py, tests/test_nav_troubleshooting.py.
          • Scout is a top-level sidebar entry, right above Wiki (request: "put the Scout section at the top level, above Wiki"). It left Troubleshooting: in Global it is the first entry of the Global block, in a device ADOM its own entry right above Operations. Same gates; a hidden Scout stays hidden.

          Fixed

          • Software Update › Purge old packs never asked for confirmation: its inline onsubmit was blocked by the CSP (script-src-attr none), so the confirm dialog never showed; it uses data-fw-confirm-form now.
          • 26 strings of the Software Update / kbpack / app-token screens rendered in English in German, Spanish, French and Italian; translated.
          • The Apps-only portal header fell back to a generic icon instead of the product mark when no theme logo is set.
          • Security (satom-audit nightly): pyasn1 pinned to 0.6.5 (four quadratic-CPU decoder CVEs in <=0.6.4, pulled unpinned by ldap3); the app sign-in link shown to administrators is built on this node's own name, not on the request's Host header.
          • Diagnose Log Collection app: the run recognised its own collection by the exact start time, which the collection thread rewrites, and failed every run with "another collection replaced this one" (found live on a1).
